A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-Harmony research. The complete main texts and appendices, including rendered figures, tables and equations, support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across five models and six reasoning benchmarks, together with component ablations, sensitivity tests and analyses of generated paraphrases.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original Reframer-scale experiments, selector comparisons, inference-only evaluations and training-signal analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix I adds an explicitly evaluated inference-only use of Self-Harmony, returning the harmonic-mean-selected answer without policy updates. The main shared Solver/Reframer training procedure, prompts, pseudo-label rule and fused multiplicative reward remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The six reasoning benchmarks and task domains are retained. Added experiments stratify existing math problems by confidence and correctness or vary models and inference settings; they do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods remain unchanged. New Table 8 adds evaluated quadratic-mean, geometric-mean (listed as Geometry) and Full Infomax selectors alongside harmonic/arithmetic aggregation and TTRL, extending the auxiliary selector comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include confidence/correctness stratification, varying Reframer sizes from 0.6B to 14B with each Solver held fixed, and inference-only evaluations with 32–256 rollouts. F1 and Spearman correlation supplement accuracy measurements. The original benchmark settings and Table 3 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands investigation of why the method works: Reframer-scale robustness in E.3, alternative selectors in H, selection without training in I, and signal quality across confidence/correctness groups in J and L. Appendix F also revises successful and problematic rewrite examples. Earlier ablations and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing checkpoint averaging and coefficient-sensitivity ranges are retained. The added correlation metrics measure signal quality rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 4 retain their numerical results, while Tables 5 and 8–10 and Figure 12 add substantial new outcomes. For example, new inference-only AMC results at 32 rollouts report 56.63% for Self-Harmony versus 54.22% for majority voting with Qwen-4B-Base. These are additional experimental results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The original proof moves from F.1 to G.1, and its uniform-view prior becomes explicit in Theorem 3.2. Substantial new derivations connect generalized means to k = 1 − lambda, introduce a K-view theorem and proof, and derive a non-uniform-prior score in G.2–G.4. E.5 also adds the reward linearization underlying additive-weight matching.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: label-free cooperative self-play, harmonic-mean pseudo-label selection, first-place performance in 28 of 30 settings and training stability. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: New discussion argues robustness to imperfect paraphrases, benefits on confidently incorrect and ambiguous examples, and applicability without training. It also interprets selector choices through variance penalties and expands the explanation of multiplicative rewards. Appendix F corrects the quantum-matrix rewrite's classification from well-formed to problematic.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub repository, clarifies independent label-free adaptation for each dataset, identifies Figure 3(b)'s Level-3 subset, and specifies additive-reward weights. Existing prompts and hyperparameter tables are unchanged; these disclosures do not establish rerunning the original experiments.

R1.justification: Related work adds references and localized positioning concerning external reward models, self-consistency preference learning, invariant risk minimization and group-invariant augmentation. Pólya and Spiro support the multi-perspective motivation. The overarching positioning as self-contained cooperative test-time learning remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions expand related work and pseudo-label interpretation, add a rewrite-examples subsection and disclosure statements, and organize theory into a dedicated appendix. Author affiliations, contact information and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: The ICLR format substantially changes text widths, typography, display sizes and placement. v2 adds the rewrite graphic in Figure 5, the multi-panel signal comparison in Figure 12, and four result tables, while revising the example tables. Many earlier figures are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Targeted selector, robustness and inference-only comparisons improve empirical scrutiny, while corrected rewrite examples and explicit reward weights improve accuracy and reproducibility of the account. The gains are limited by weaknesses in the additions: G.3 unjustifiably approximates Bernoulli entropy by its probability, and Table 9's non-decreasing-performance caption conflicts with some reported decreases. The central benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
